title: Minneapolis as a regional meeting place; the Pettiford family
summary: They discuss Minneapolis as the music hub near Omaha and Des Moines and Thomas recalls meeting the Pettiford family, including Oscar and Killer, in Oklahoma.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: So you met Prez in...
I met him in Minneapolis.
You met him in Minneapolis.
Mmm-hmm.
That was like a meeting place out there, wasn't it.
Yeah, because Minneapolis was the closest town to Des Moines, Omaha and all that...
And it was a populous(?) city.

Yeah, and it was a Twin City. It was a big town. It was the Twin Cities. And they had a lot of music going there, and you could...and I just... I think Eddie Barefield played with Clarence Johnson. I got to talking with Eddie one day, boy, and...
Remember a fellow named Jack Oglesby? Remember him?
No, but I remember that bass player from there?
Who, Oscar Pettiford?
No.
Oh, you're talking about...
Thomas - 48
Well, I met the Pettifords in Oklahoma originally. I met Oscar when he was...
You meant Adolphus Allsbrook.
Yeah. Right. Oscar played bass horn. And man, he was so little, I couldn't see how he could even play the bass horn. That's the first time we met. Then I knew all his sisters... He had a...
One of them played drums.
Yeah. And he had a brother... Did he have a brother that played piano?
Killer, yeah.
Boy, he played the heck out that.
He looked a lot like Coleman Hawkins.
But he was scared to leave Minneapolis.
I remember him.
Yeah, I knew all those guys. They came there a little late.
And one brother played trumpet.
Yeah. Yeah, I caught the whole... I went to Oklahoma, to (?) one day, somebody was telling me about the band...
[PAUSE, INTERRUPTION]
I was talking about how I met Lester in Minneapolis. I rambled off later on when I saw Lester with King Oliver.
